creators.name: Mike Y. Chen
creators.role: Professor of Computer Science, National Taiwan University; directs the NTU HCI Lab
creators.role_zh: 台湾大学资讯工程学系教授，主持台大人机交互实验室
creators.bio: HCI researcher whose lab builds mobile, wearable and audio interfaces and tests them in everyday settings.
creators.bio_zh: 人机交互研究者，他的实验室开发移动、可穿戴与声音界面，并在日常环境中测试。
creators.why: His lab's GreenAR uses personal audio AR to put birdsong and insect sounds back into city streets.
creators.why_zh: 他的实验室开发的 GreenAR 用个人音频增强现实，把鸟鸣和虫声放回城市街道。

creators.name: Chang Hee Lee
creators.role: Associate Professor, Department of Industrial Design, KAIST
creators.role_zh: 韩国科学技术院（KAIST）工业设计系副教授
creators.bio: Industrial design researcher working on tangible and ambient interfaces for everyday life.
creators.bio_zh: 工业设计研究者，研究面向日常生活的实体与环境式界面。
creators.why: His group's TreeB612 links a person at home to one distant tree without screens or sound.
creators.why_zh: 他的团队设计的 TreeB612 不用屏幕也不用声音，把家中的人与远处的一棵树连接起来。

creators.name: Lei Xia
creators.role: Design researcher, College of Design and Innovation, Tongji University
creators.role_zh: 同济大学设计创意学院设计研究者
creators.bio: Designs immersive and sensory experiences for environmental communication, from VR wetlands to air-quality wearables.
creators.bio_zh: 为环境传播设计沉浸式与多感官体验，从虚拟现实湿地到空气质量可穿戴设备。
creators.why: The Wetland Quest shows how scale-shifting VR can make people care about frogs, toads and snakes they usually avoid.
creators.why_zh: 《湿地探索》展示了改变尺度的虚拟现实如何让人关心平时回避的蛙、蟾蜍和蛇。

creators.name: Zhuying Li
creators.role: Associate Professor, School of Computer Science and Engineering, Southeast University
creators.role_zh: 东南大学计算机科学与工程学院副教授
creators.bio: HCI researcher (formerly at Monash University's Exertion Games Lab) who designs playful systems for wellbeing and human–nature interaction.
creators.bio_zh: 人机交互研究者（曾在莫纳什大学 Exertion Games Lab），设计面向身心健康和人与自然交互的趣味系统。
creators.why: Her group produced several 2026 human–nature interaction systems: NatureCapture, GreenCompass and a study of how blind people experience nature.
creators.why_zh: 她的团队在 2026 年发表了多项人与自然交互研究：NatureCapture、GreenCompass，以及盲人如何体验自然的研究。

creators.name: Piumi Perera
creators.role: PhD researcher, School of Computing and Information Systems, University of Melbourne
creators.role_zh: 墨尔本大学计算与信息系统学院博士研究者
creators.bio: Studies how everyday digital tools shape people's visits to nature and how HCI can mediate human–nature relations.
creators.bio_zh: 研究日常数字工具如何影响人们走进自然的经历，以及人机交互如何中介人与自然的关系。
creators.why: Her CHI 2026 field studies map when phones help and when they get in the way of experiencing nature.
creators.why_zh: 她在 CHI 2026 发表的实地研究梳理了手机何时帮助、何时妨碍人们体验自然。

creators.name: Bakhtawar Aurangzeb Khan
creators.role: Researcher, Gamification Group, Tampere University
creators.role_zh: 坦佩雷大学游戏化研究组研究者
creators.bio: Researches virtual nature, games and wellbeing.
creators.bio_zh: 研究虚拟自然、游戏与身心健康。
creators.why: Led a systematic review of 124 virtual-nature studies that asks HCI to move beyond short stress relief.
creators.why_zh: 主导了一项涵盖 124 项虚拟自然研究的系统综述，呼吁人机交互不止于短时减压。

creators.name: Zhao Zhao
creators.role: Assistant Professor, School of Computer Science, University of Guelph
creators.role_zh: 圭尔夫大学计算机科学学院助理教授
creators.bio: HCI researcher working on ambient and personal technologies for engagement and wellbeing.
creators.bio_zh: 人机交互研究者，研究促进参与和身心健康的环境式与个人技术。
creators.why: Her group's WildCompanion keeps people quietly connected to the wild animal they adopted through a conservation charity.
creators.why_zh: 她的团队开发的 WildCompanion 让人与自己通过保护机构认养的野生动物保持安静而持续的联系。

creators.name: Dana Habeeb
creators.role: Assistant Professor, Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering, Indiana University
creators.role_zh: 印第安纳大学 Luddy 信息、计算与工程学院助理教授
creators.bio: Researches urban heat, environmental sensing and participatory design of civic data infrastructure.
creators.bio_zh: 研究城市高温、环境感测，以及市民数据基础设施的参与式设计。
creators.why: She co-designs environmental sensor networks with community growers instead of deploying them top-down.
creators.why_zh: 她与社区种植者共同设计环境传感器网络，而不是自上而下地布设。

creators.name: Julia McKenna
creators.role: Researcher, Northwestern University; works with Ojibwe Tribal partners on Manoomin (wild rice) stewardship tools
creators.role_zh: 西北大学研究者；与奥吉布瓦部落伙伴合作开发野生稻（Manoomin）守护工具
creators.bio: Works on Indigenous-led environmental sensing and data tools in the Great Lakes region.
creators.bio_zh: 在美国五大湖地区从事由原住民主导的环境感测与数据工具研究。
creators.why: Her team's Makak sensors and Noondawind dashboard show how environmental tech can serve Tribal data sovereignty and a culturally central plant.
creators.why_zh: 她的团队开发的 Makak 传感器和 Noondawind 数据平台，展示了环境技术如何服务于部落数据主权和一种文化上至关重要的植物。

creators.name: Yanxia Li
creators.role: PhD researcher, School of Computer Science, Queensland University of Technology
creators.role_zh: 昆士兰科技大学计算机科学学院博士研究者
creators.bio: Studies how young children notice nature in childcare food gardens and how technology could support it.
creators.bio_zh: 研究幼儿如何在托育机构的食物花园中留意自然，以及技术如何支持这种留意。
creators.why: Her work turns 'slow noticing' into concrete design opportunities for children's nature technology.
creators.why_zh: 她把“慢慢留意”转化为面向儿童自然技术的具体设计机会。

creators.name: Robert Soden
creators.role: Assistant Professor, Computer Science and School of the Environment, University of Toronto
creators.role_zh: 多伦多大学计算机科学系与环境学院助理教授
creators.bio: HCI and STS researcher working on climate, disaster risk and environmental data.
creators.bio_zh: 人机交互与科学技术研究（STS）学者，研究气候、灾害风险与环境数据。
creators.why: The Toronto Water Atlas he led shows design keeping many versions of 'water' alive instead of one policy dataset.
creators.why_zh: 他主持的多伦多水图集展示了设计如何让“水”的多种存在方式并存，而不是只剩一种政策数据。

creators.name: Sebastian Prost
creators.role: Lecturer, Centre for HCI Design, City St George's, University of London
creators.role_zh: 伦敦城市圣乔治大学人机交互设计中心讲师
creators.bio: Researches food systems, agroecology and grassroots technology from an HCI perspective.
creators.bio_zh: 从人机交互角度研究食物系统、农业生态学与基层技术。
creators.why: He argues for farmer-led digital tools that support agroecology instead of industrial agri-tech.
creators.why_zh: 他主张由农民主导、支持农业生态学的数字工具，而非工业化的农业科技。

creators.name: Jae-eun Shin
creators.role: Researcher, Graduate School of Information, Yonsei University
creators.role_zh: 延世大学信息研究生院研究者
creators.bio: Studies extended reality through posthuman and more-than-human theory.
creators.bio_zh: 以后人类与超越人类理论研究扩展现实。
creators.why: Offers a vocabulary for designing XR worlds, bodies and interactions beyond the human.
creators.why_zh: 为超越人类视角的 XR 世界、身体与交互设计提供了一套词汇。

creators.name: Shuran Fan
creators.role: Design researcher, Wuhan University
creators.role_zh: 武汉大学设计研究者
creators.bio: Designs wearable and zoomorphic interfaces for everyday nature experiences.
creators.bio_zh: 为日常自然体验设计可穿戴与仿生形态的界面。
creators.why: Her Perch wearable borrows a sparrow's attention to point people at the nature around them.
creators.why_zh: 她设计的 Perch 可穿戴设备借用麻雀的注意力，把人的目光引向身边的自然。

creators.name: Sihan Wang
creators.role: Design researcher, School of Creativity and Art, ShanghaiTech University
creators.role_zh: 上海科技大学创意与艺术学院设计研究者
creators.bio: Designs speculative, post-anthropocentric artefacts for urban ecological awareness.
creators.bio_zh: 设计面向城市生态意识的思辨性、去人类中心的人造物。
creators.why: InterYard imagines electronic plant species that keep city dwellers in step with biological rhythms.
creators.why_zh: InterYard 设想了一组电子植物物种，让城市居民重新跟上生物的节律。

creators.name: Tram Thi Minh Tran
creators.role: Researcher, Design Lab, School of Architecture, Design and Planning, University of Sydney
creators.role_zh: 悉尼大学建筑、设计与规划学院设计实验室研究者
creators.bio: HCI researcher working on immersive technologies, urban robots and more-than-human participation in planning.
creators.bio_zh: 人机交互研究者，研究沉浸式技术、城市机器人，以及规划中的超越人类参与。
creators.why: Her team probes how voice agents and XR should 'speak for' species in crisis planning, and where that goes wrong.
creators.why_zh: 她的团队探讨语音代理和 XR 在危机规划中应如何“替”物种发声，以及哪里会出问题。

creators.name: Ceren Ozgen
creators.role: Assistant Professor, Department of Design, University of Texas at Austin
creators.role_zh: 得克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校设计系助理教授
creators.bio: Designer-researcher who develops embodied, movement-based workshop methods for more-than-human design.
creators.bio_zh: 设计研究者，发展面向超越人类设计的具身、基于身体动作的工作坊方法。
creators.why: Her workshops let people feel climate and other species through movement before looking at data.
creators.why_zh: 她的工作坊让人先通过身体动作感受气候与其他物种，再去看数据。

creators.name: Supratim Pait
creators.role: Researcher, Digital Media, Georgia Institute of Technology
creators.role_zh: 佐治亚理工学院数字媒体研究者
creators.bio: Designs tangible interfaces that connect local ecologies with social and historical archives.
creators.bio_zh: 设计把在地生态与社会、历史档案联系起来的实体界面。
creators.why: His Entangled Histories Radio lets a city tree's sensed conditions select Civil Rights Movement recordings, linking environmental and civil rights justice.
creators.why_zh: 他的《纠缠历史电台》让一棵城市树木的感测状态挑选民权运动录音，把环境正义与民权正义联系起来。

creators.name: Asimina Vasalou
creators.role: Professor, UCL Knowledge Lab, University College London
creators.role_zh: 伦敦大学学院（UCL）知识实验室教授
creators.bio: Researches children's learning, play and making with technology.
creators.bio_zh: 研究儿童借助技术进行的学习、游戏与制作。
creators.why: Her Hybrid Nature Crafts combine leaves and light so children make with nature, not only in it.
creators.why_zh: 她提出的“混合自然手工”把树叶与光结合，让儿童与自然一起创作，而不只是在自然中创作。

creators.name: Yuxi Wu
creators.role: Researcher, Khoury College of Computer Sciences, Northeastern University
creators.role_zh: 东北大学 Khoury 计算机科学学院研究者
creators.bio: HCI researcher using autoethnography to study outdoor recreation, technology and more-than-human encounters.
creators.bio_zh: 人机交互研究者，用自我民族志研究户外活动、技术与超越人类的相遇。
creators.why: Her long-distance hiking study shows how physical disorientation keeps forcing hikers to notice the more-than-human.
creators.why_zh: 她对长距离徒步的研究显示，身体上的迷失如何一再迫使徒步者留意超越人类的世界。

creators.name: Shruti Rao
creators.role: PhD researcher, Informatics Institute, University of Amsterdam
creators.role_zh: 阿姆斯特丹大学信息学院博士研究者
creators.bio: Architect and HCI researcher working on biophilic design and human–building interaction.
creators.bio_zh: 建筑师与人机交互研究者，研究亲生物设计和人与建筑的交互。
creators.why: She turns biophilic architecture into an interaction design framework for indoor spaces.
creators.why_zh: 她把亲生物建筑的思路转化为室内空间的交互设计框架。

creators.name: Valentina Nisi
creators.role: Associate Professor, Instituto Superior Técnico, University of Lisbon; researcher at ITI/LARSyS
creators.role_zh: 里斯本大学高等理工学院副教授，ITI/LARSyS 研究者
creators.bio: Interaction design researcher working on transmedia storytelling, ocean literacy and posthuman HCI, long based in Madeira.
creators.bio_zh: 交互设计研究者，研究跨媒体叙事、海洋素养与后人类人机交互，长期在马德拉开展工作。
creators.why: Her group produces a steady stream of more-than-human methods and artefacts around oceans, seaweed and time.
creators.why_zh: 她的团队围绕海洋、海藻与时间，持续产出超越人类的设计方法与作品。

creators.name: Fernanda Soares da Costa
creators.role: PhD researcher, ITI/LARSyS, Instituto Superior Técnico, University of Lisbon
creators.role_zh: 里斯本大学高等理工学院 ITI/LARSyS 博士研究者
creators.bio: Designer working with sea-derived biomaterials such as agar and shells through first-person making.
creators.bio_zh: 以第一人称的制作方式，研究琼脂、贝壳等来自海洋的生物材料的设计者。
creators.why: Her SeaFoam journey shows material design as a way of attuning to coastal ecologies.
creators.why_zh: 她的 SeaFoam 制作过程，展示了材料设计如何成为与海岸生态调谐的方式。

creators.name: Lizette Reitsma
creators.role: Senior Lecturer in Interaction Design, School of Arts and Communication, Malmö University
creators.role_zh: 马尔默大学艺术与传播学院交互设计高级讲师
creators.bio: Participatory design researcher working with Indigenous and local communities on climate knowledge.
creators.bio_zh: 参与式设计研究者，与原住民和地方社区合作研究气候知识。
creators.why: Her Indigenous Climate Observatories use hand-made blankets to weave local and scientific climate knowledge together.
creators.why_zh: 她的“原住民气候观测站”用手工毯子把地方知识与科学的气候知识编织在一起。

creators.name: Karey Helms
creators.role: Assistant Professor, Umeå Institute of Design, Umeå University
creators.role_zh: 于默奥大学设计学院助理教授
creators.bio: Interaction design researcher known for first-person design with the body, family life and everyday care.
creators.bio_zh: 交互设计研究者，以围绕身体、家庭生活与日常照料的第一人称设计研究而知名。
creators.why: She asks where children are in more-than-human design and shows it through a year of seasonal nature crafts.
creators.why_zh: 她追问儿童在超越人类设计中的位置，并通过一整年的季节性自然手工来回答。

creators.name: Youp Ferket
creators.role: PhD researcher, Department of Industrial Design, Eindhoven University of Technology
creators.role_zh: 埃因霍温理工大学工业设计系博士研究者
creators.bio: Designer-researcher developing drawing and sketching as methods for noticing in more-than-human design.
creators.bio_zh: 设计研究者，把绘画与速写发展为超越人类设计中的“留意”方法。
creators.why: His guided sketching practice turns observational drawing into a structured way of noticing other species.
creators.why_zh: 他的引导式速写练习，把观察性绘画变成一种有结构地留意其他物种的方法。

creators.name: Bhavani Seetharaman
creators.role: PhD researcher, Computational Media, University of California, Santa Cruz
creators.role_zh: 加州大学圣克鲁兹分校计算媒体系博士研究者
creators.bio: Researches speculative design, outdoor recreation technology and environmental values.
creators.bio_zh: 研究思辨设计、户外休闲技术与环境价值。
creators.why: Her Otter 841 project redesigns surf and recreation apps around the needs of a famous sea otter.
creators.why_zh: 她的“841 号海獭”项目，围绕一只著名海獭的需要重新设计冲浪与户外休闲应用。

creators.name: Francesca Zeccara
creators.role: Design researcher, Department of Design, Politecnico di Milano
creators.role_zh: 米兰理工大学设计系设计研究者
creators.bio: Researches living materials and participatory approaches to biodesign.
creators.bio_zh: 研究活体材料以及生物设计中的参与式方法。
creators.why: She proposes treating living materials as stakeholders in participatory design ('bio-inclusive design').
creators.why_zh: 她提出在参与式设计中把活体材料当作利益相关者（“生物包容设计”）。

creators.name: Carlos Roberto Torres-Parra
creators.role: Professor, Department of Design, Pontificia Universidad Javeriana
creators.role_zh: 哥伦比亚哈维里亚纳天主教大学设计系教授
creators.bio: Design researcher working on critical games and intercultural co-creation.
creators.bio_zh: 设计研究者，研究批判性游戏与跨文化共创。
creators.why: Co-created Hizca, a video game about the páramo, with the Muisca community of Sesquilé.
creators.why_zh: 与塞斯基莱的穆伊斯卡社区共同创作了关于帕拉莫高原的电子游戏 Hizca。

creators.name: Joni Salminen
creators.role: Associate Professor, School of Marketing and Communication, University of Vaasa
creators.role_zh: 瓦萨大学市场与传播学院副教授
creators.bio: Researches personas, data-driven persona generation and how people perceive them.
creators.bio_zh: 研究人物角色（persona）、数据驱动的角色生成以及人们如何感知角色。
creators.why: Adapted the widely used Persona Perception Scale so non-human personas can be evaluated on their own terms.
creators.why_zh: 改编了被广泛使用的人物角色感知量表，使非人类角色能按其自身特点被评估。

creators.name: Tom Metcalfe
creators.role: Researcher, School of Computer Science, University of St Andrews
creators.role_zh: 圣安德鲁斯大学计算机科学学院研究者
creators.bio: Design researcher working on posthumanism, new materialism and research through design.
creators.bio_zh: 设计研究者，研究后人类主义、新物质主义与设计研究（RtD）。
creators.why: Argues that much of HCI's 'posthuman turn' changes vocabulary without changing method.
creators.why_zh: 他指出，人机交互中所谓的“后人类转向”很多只是换了词汇，而没有改变方法。

creators.name: Ylva Fernaeus
creators.role: Professor, Umeå Institute of Design, Umeå University
creators.role_zh: 于默奥大学设计学院教授
creators.bio: Interaction design researcher known for work on tangible interaction, robots, craft and the history of HCI.
creators.bio_zh: 交互设计研究者，以实体交互、机器人、手工艺和人机交互史的研究知名。
creators.why: She names recurring design tropes (The Tortured Plant, The Cyberpunk Wearable, The Faked Human) that expose confusions in more-than-human design.
creators.why_zh: 她归纳出超越人类设计中反复出现的设计套路（受折磨的植物、赛博朋克可穿戴、伪装的人），揭示其中的概念混乱。

creators.name: Verindi Vekemans
creators.role: Design researcher, Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering, Delft University of Technology
creators.role_zh: 代尔夫特理工大学工业设计工程学院设计研究者
creators.bio: Researches how designers can observe, describe and work with self-healing in living materials.
creators.bio_zh: 研究设计者如何观察、描述并运用活体材料的自我修复。
creators.why: Her X_Heal Toolkit treats self-healing as an expressive, temporal behaviour designers can annotate and reinterpret.
creators.why_zh: 她的 X_Heal 工具包把自我修复视为设计者可以标注和重新诠释的、具表现力的时间性行为。

creators.name: Ines Weigand
creators.role: Designer and researcher, Berlin University of the Arts (UdK Berlin)
creators.role_zh: 柏林艺术大学设计师与研究者
creators.bio: Works on experiential design pedagogy that translates environmental humanities into bodily experience.
creators.bio_zh: 从事体验式设计教学，把环境人文学的理论转化为身体经验。
creators.why: Her 'Becoming humus' workshops have people turn their own urine into fertiliser to feel planetary nutrient cycles.
creators.why_zh: 她的“成为腐殖质”工作坊让人把自己的尿液变成肥料，从而亲身感受行星尺度的养分循环。

creators.name: Michael (Miek) Dunbar
creators.role: Lecturer, RMIT University; co-leads the Greater Melbourne City Portrait with Regen Melbourne
creators.role_zh: 皇家墨尔本理工大学讲师；与 Regen Melbourne 共同主持“大墨尔本城市画像”项目
creators.bio: Designer working on more-than-human datasets, data fabulation and regenerative city futures.
creators.bio_zh: 研究超越人类数据集、数据虚构与再生性城市未来的设计者。
creators.why: His Kin Bank uses synthetic data to imagine the 'transactions' between people and the non-humans a city depends on.
creators.why_zh: 他的 Kin Bank 用合成数据想象人与城市所依赖的非人类之间的“交易”。

creators.name: Yibo Meng
creators.role: Design researcher, Tsinghua University
creators.role_zh: 清华大学设计研究者
creators.bio: Researches interaction design for human–plant relations and empathy-oriented experiences.
creators.bio_zh: 研究人与植物关系的交互设计以及以共情为导向的体验。
creators.why: His office-plant biofeedback artefact turns workplace plants from decoration into co-workers that ask for care.
creators.why_zh: 他设计的办公室植物生物反馈装置，让职场植物从装饰品变成需要照料的“同事”。

creators.name: Ruth Neubauer
creators.role: Design researcher, New Design University St. Pölten and Loughborough University London
creators.role_zh: 圣珀尔滕新设计大学与拉夫堡大学伦敦校区设计研究者
creators.bio: Designer exploring low-tech, eco-social prototypes and care-based innovation.
creators.bio_zh: 探索低技术、生态-社会原型与以照料为基础的创新的设计者。
creators.why: Her 'careful configurations' (wooden fridges, moss bathrooms, communal hydration) are an alternative to 'smart' tech.
creators.why_zh: 她的“细心的配置”（木制冰箱、苔藓浴室、共享饮水）是“智能”技术之外的另一种选择。

creators.name: Corinne Okada Takara
creators.role: Artist, STEAM educator and designer, Okada Design
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、STEAM 教育者与设计师，Okada Design
creators.bio: Native Hawaiian artist-educator known for community bioquilts, lauhala circuitry and sustainable making.
creators.bio_zh: 夏威夷原住民艺术家与教育者，以社区生物拼布、露兜树叶编织电路和可持续制作著称。
creators.why: She frames play design as reciprocal care with plants and microbes, grounded in the Hawaiian values of pilina and kuleana.
creators.why_zh: 她以夏威夷的 pilina（互惠关系）与 kuleana（责任）为基础，把游戏设计视为与植物和微生物之间的互惠照料。

creators.name: Delphine Lewandowski
creators.role: Architect and researcher, Pennsylvania State University
creators.role_zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学建筑师与研究者
creators.bio: Architect researching biodiverse building envelopes and environmental ethics in design.
creators.bio_zh: 研究生物多样性建筑围护结构与设计中的环境伦理的建筑师。
creators.why: Her biodiverse wall prototypes test what it means to design buildings that plants and other species colonise on their own terms.
creators.why_zh: 她的生物多样性墙体原型，检验设计一座让植物和其他物种按自己的方式定居的建筑意味着什么。

creators.name: Gillian Russell
creators.role: Associate Professor, School of Interactive Arts and Technology, Simon Fraser University
creators.role_zh: 西蒙弗雷泽大学交互艺术与技术学院副教授
creators.bio: Design researcher working on futures, co-speculation and more-than-human design.
creators.bio_zh: 研究未来、共同思辨与超越人类设计的设计研究者。
creators.why: Her Monsters of Marine Debris kit turns citizen beach-litter data into ocean futures-making.
creators.why_zh: 她的“海洋垃圾怪兽”工具包把公民海滩垃圾数据变成塑造海洋未来的材料。

creators.name: Elisabet M. Nilsson
creators.role: Associate Professor, School of Arts and Communication, Malmö University
creators.role_zh: 马尔默大学艺术与传播学院副教授
creators.bio: Interaction design researcher working on design education, futures literacy and more-than-human perspectives.
creators.bio_zh: 研究设计教育、未来素养与超越人类视角的交互设计研究者。
creators.why: Leads a collection of classroom activities for teaching more-than-human perspectives to technology design students.
creators.why_zh: 主导整理了一套课堂活动，用于向技术设计专业学生讲授超越人类的视角。

creators.name: Katia Zolotovsky
creators.role: Assistant Professor, Art + Design (joint appointment in Chemistry and Chemical Biology), Northeastern University; directs the BioInteractive Design Lab (BInD)
creators.role_zh: 东北大学艺术与设计系助理教授（兼任化学与化学生物学系），主持生物交互设计实验室（BInD）
creators.bio: Designer and biologist leading a lab that combines synthetic biology, textiles and fabrication.
creators.bio_zh: 设计师与生物学家，带领一个结合合成生物学、纺织与制造的实验室。
creators.why: Her Living Textiles platform puts engineered bacterial biosensors into fabric so clothes can sense and respond through living cells.
creators.why_zh: 她的“活体纺织品”平台把工程化细菌生物传感器织入面料，让衣物通过活细胞感知与回应。

creators.name: Petra Jääskeläinen
creators.role: Researcher, Division of Media Technology and Interaction Design, KTH Royal Institute of Technology
creators.role_zh: 瑞典皇家理工学院媒体技术与交互设计系研究者
creators.bio: Researches creative AI, its environmental impacts and more-than-human perspectives on creativity.
creators.bio_zh: 研究创意 AI、其环境影响，以及关于创造力的超越人类视角。
creators.why: Proposes shifting creative-AI design from human creativity to 'sympoiesis', making-with situated ecologies.
creators.why_zh: 提出把创意 AI 的设计从“人的创造力”转向“共生创作”，即与在地生态一起创作。

creators.name: Svenja Keune
creators.role: Senior Lecturer in Textile Design, Swedish School of Textiles, University of Borås
creators.role_zh: 布罗斯大学瑞典纺织学院纺织设计高级讲师
creators.bio: Textile designer working on textiles for and with plants and insects; co-organiser of the I.N.S.E.C.T. summer camps.
creators.bio_zh: 研究为植物与昆虫、并与它们一起设计纺织品的纺织设计师；I.N.S.E.C.T. 夏令营的共同组织者。
creators.why: The I.N.S.E.C.T. camps develop embodied methods for designers to meet insect worlds, here through vibration.
creators.why_zh: I.N.S.E.C.T. 夏令营为设计者发展进入昆虫世界的具身方法，这一次通过“振动”。

creators.name: Yule Chen
creators.role: Design researcher, School of Design, Hunan University
creators.role_zh: 湖南大学设计艺术学院设计研究者
creators.bio: Researches human–plant interaction and bio-sensory coupling for wellbeing.
creators.bio_zh: 研究人与植物交互以及面向身心健康的生物感官耦合。
creators.why: Built a meditation system in which a living plant's photosynthesis sets the soundscape that guides breathing.
creators.why_zh: 设计了一个冥想系统，由活体植物的光合作用生成引导呼吸的声景。

creators.name: Gianluca Giabardo
creators.role: Designer, baker and doctoral researcher, Aalto University
creators.role_zh: 设计师、面包师，阿尔托大学博士研究者
creators.bio: Practice-led researcher who runs a sourdough bakery as a site for thinking about form, making and conviviality.
creators.bio_zh: 以实践为导向的研究者，把自己经营的酸面包烘焙坊当作思考形式、制作与共生的场所。
creators.why: Uses sourdough, a living culture, to show design as attunement rather than domestication.
creators.why_zh: 借助酸面团这一活的菌群，展示设计是一种调谐，而不是驯化。

creators.name: Olivier Cotsaftis
creators.role: Design researcher and educator working on regenerative and relational design
creators.role_zh: 研究再生性设计与关系性设计的设计研究者与教育者
creators.bio: Writes on language, speculative materialism and how designers position themselves toward nature.
creators.bio_zh: 研究语言、思辨唯物主义，以及设计者如何定位自己与自然的关系。
creators.why: His five prepositions (designing about, with, for, as and on nature) give designers a quick test of their stance toward the living world.
creators.why_zh: 他提出的五个介词——关于、与、为、作为、在自然之上设计——为设计者提供了检验自身对待生命世界之立场的简便方法。

creators.name: Melisa Miranda Correa
creators.role: Designer and researcher working with Indigenous communities in northern Chile
creators.role_zh: 与智利北部原住民社区合作的设计师与研究者
creators.bio: Practices pluriversal, ontological design through visual artefacts made with Atacameño communities.
creators.bio_zh: 通过与阿塔卡梅尼奥社区共同制作视觉作品，实践多元世界的本体论设计。
creators.why: Her 'esquejes' (plant cuttings) method lets visual artefacts root and grow in communities beyond the researcher's authorship.
creators.why_zh: 她的“插枝”（esquejes）方法让视觉作品在社区中生根生长，超出研究者的作者身份。

works.title: GreenAR: Restoring Urban Natural Soundscapes with Personal Audio AR
works.description: A location-aware audio AR system that plays birdsong and insect sounds placed on the real greenery around a walker in the city, tested in three field studies including a week-long deployment in five countries.
works.description_zh: 一个基于位置的音频增强现实系统：在城市步行时，把鸟鸣和虫声放到行人周围真实的绿地上播放。研究包括三项实地测试，其中一项在五个国家部署了一周。
works.idea_en: Restoring missing nature sounds can make people notice both the greenery that is there and the greenery that is missing.
works.idea_zh: 补回消失的自然声音，能让人既注意到身边的绿地，也注意到缺失的绿地。
works.method: Biophony is composed from OpenStreetMap green areas and spatialised in headphones with GPS-error-tolerant placement; studies measured nature connectedness, eco-awareness and reflection.
works.method_zh: 根据 OpenStreetMap 上的绿地生成生物声景，并以容忍 GPS 误差的方式在耳机中做空间定位；研究测量了自然联结、生态意识与反思。

paper.title: Reacquainting with Everyday Urban Nature: Exploring Natural Soundscape Restoration with Personal Audio AR

works.title: TreeB612
works.description: A screenless, soundless device that pairs a person at home with one chosen tree far away; a 7-day diary deployment with 10 people looked at how this quiet link shaped everyday attention to the tree.
works.description_zh: 一个没有屏幕也没有声音的装置，把家中的人与远处选定的一棵树配对；研究让 10 位参与者使用 7 天并写日记，观察这种安静的连接如何影响他们日常对这棵树的关注。
works.idea_en: A remote link to one specific living tree, felt through light and touch rather than media, can invite imagination and care.
works.idea_zh: 通过光与触感而非影像与声音，与一棵具体的树远程相连，可以唤起想象与照料之心。
works.method: A transmitter unit placed at the tree sends signals over long-range radio (LoRa) to a glowing receiver at home (likely reflecting tree-side sensing); survey (N=55) informed the design.
works.method_zh: 放在树旁的发送装置通过远距离无线电（LoRa）把信号传到家中会发光的接收器（很可能反映树旁的感测数据）；设计参考了 55 人的问卷。

paper.title: TreeB612: Exploring Interactions for Distant Human–Nature Engagement

works.title: The Wetland Quest
works.description: A VR experience set in a Shanghai wetland where players shift to the scale of local amphibians and reptiles; with 62 participants it raised species knowledge and reduced aversion to these animals.
works.description_zh: 一个以上海湿地为场景的虚拟现实体验，玩家被缩放到本地两栖与爬行动物的尺度；62 位参与者的研究显示，它提升了物种知识，并减少了对这些动物的反感。
works.idea_en: Changing your body scale is a strong way to build empathy for overlooked, even disliked, species.
works.idea_zh: 改变身体尺度，是对被忽视甚至被厌恶的物种建立共情的有力方式。
works.method: Embodiment and scale-shift mechanics in VR; mixed-methods evaluation with knowledge tests, validated attitude scales, observation and interviews.
works.method_zh: 在虚拟现实中使用具身与尺度变换机制；以知识测试、标准态度量表、观察和访谈进行混合方法评估。

paper.title: The Wetland Quest: Fostering Empathy and Literacy for Urban Herpetofauna Through VR Wetland Exploration

works.title: NatureCapture
works.description: A multi-user system where people photograph leaves, stones and other natural things on their daily routes, turn them into 3D models and place them together in a shared VR nature space.
works.description_zh: 一个多人系统：人们在日常路线上拍下树叶、石头等自然物，把它们转成 3D 模型，再一起放进共享的虚拟现实自然空间。
works.idea_en: Let virtual nature be built from the real nature people actually encountered, so the two keep feeding each other.
works.idea_zh: 让虚拟自然由人们真正遇见的真实自然搭建起来，使二者相互滋养。
works.method: Phone capture of natural elements is converted to interactive 3D models and assembled collaboratively in VR; a two-week within-subjects study measured nature connectedness, emotion regulation and social closeness.
works.method_zh: 用手机采集自然物并转成可交互的 3D 模型，在虚拟现实中协作布置；为期两周的被试内研究测量了自然联结、情绪调节与社会亲密感。

paper.title: NatureCapture: Transforming Real-World Nature into Shared VR Experiences for Deepened Human-Nature Connection

works.title: GreenCompass
works.description: A social mobile app that suggests short nature encounters near you that fit into gaps in the day, with playful, adaptive tasks; in a four-week study with 40 people it raised nature relatedness and outdoor activity more than simple reminders.
works.description_zh: 一款社交手机应用，根据日程空隙推荐附近的短暂自然接触，并配以有趣、可调整的小任务；为期四周、40 人参与的研究显示，它比单纯的提醒更能提升自然关联感和户外活动。
works.idea_en: Nature connection can be woven into urban micro-moments instead of waiting for a trip to the wild.
works.idea_zh: 与自然的联结可以编织进城市生活的零碎时刻，而不必等到一次远行。
works.method: Context-aware scheduling plus gamified, adaptive tasks and group play; field study against a reminder-based baseline.
works.method_zh: 结合情境感知的日程安排、游戏化的自适应任务与群体互动；与只发提醒的对照组进行实地比较。

paper.title: GreenCompass: Weaving Playful Nature Engagement into Urban Micro-Moments through Context-Aware Gamification

works.title: Capra in Long-Term Use: Becoming Watchful on the Trail and at Home
works.description: A multi-year first-person study in which three researchers hiked with and lived with Capra, a slow device for capturing and later revisiting hikes; their attention shifted from capturing striking sights to noticing more on the trail and when looking back.
works.description_zh: 一项持续数年的第一人称研究：三位研究者带着 Capra 徒步并与它共同生活。Capra 是一个用于记录并在日后重温徒步的“慢”设备；他们的注意力从拍下醒目景象，转向在步道上和回看时留意更多细节。
works.idea_en: Designing for occasional, indefinite use lets hiking data grow into a practice of noticing nature over years.
works.idea_zh: 为偶尔、无期限的使用而设计，能让徒步数据在多年里慢慢变成留意自然的习惯。
works.method: Long-term autobiographical deployment of a custom capture device and home viewer by researchers with different hiking paces, places and life stages.
works.method_zh: 由徒步频率、地点和人生阶段各不相同的研究者，长期自我部署一套定制记录设备和家用浏览器。

paper.title: Becoming Watchful on the Trail and at Home: Understanding Experiential Outcomes of Capra in Long-Term Use

works.title: "I'm here to see nature, not spend more time on my phone!"
works.description: A field study of 30 adults in an urban nature park using tools from a camera to a plant-ID app to a site-specific AR app, describing how technology becomes obtrusive in nature and the tactics people use to keep it in its place.
works.description_zh: 一项在城市自然公园中进行的实地研究：30 位成年人使用从相机、植物识别应用到场地 AR 应用等不同工具，研究描述了技术在自然中如何变得扰人，以及人们如何让它“各安其位”。
works.idea_en: Obtrusiveness comes less from how interactive a tool is than from a mismatch with how people want to be in nature.
works.idea_zh: 技术是否扰人，与其说取决于交互强度，不如说取决于它是否与人想要的自然体验相冲突。
works.method: Field observation and interviews across four levels of interactive intensity; analysis yields seven facets of obtrusiveness and six management tactics (abstaining, limiting, minimising, deferring, delegating, conforming).
works.method_zh: 在四种交互强度下进行实地观察与访谈；分析得出七种扰人体验和六种应对策略（放弃、限制、减少、推迟、委托、顺从）。

paper.title: "I'm here to see nature, not spend more time on my phone!": A Study of Technological Obtrusiveness and How it is Managed in an Urban Nature Setting

works.title: The Technology–Nature Paradox
works.description: Interviews with 30 people about the apps and devices they bring before, during and after visits to nature, identifying six modes of nature engagement (adventure, aesthetic, ambient, enquiry, escape, novelty) and the tools each mode calls for.
works.description_zh: 对 30 人的访谈，了解他们在走进自然之前、之中和之后使用的应用与设备，归纳出六种与自然相处的模式（探险、审美、氛围、探究、逃离、新奇）以及每种模式对应的工具。
works.idea_en: People go to nature to escape technology yet carefully assemble technology to do it: design should fit the mode of engagement.
works.idea_zh: 人们去自然中逃离技术，却又精心组合技术来实现这件事：设计应当契合人们与自然相处的模式。
works.method: In-depth qualitative interviews analysed by engagement mode and by visit phase (before, during, after).
works.method_zh: 深度定性访谈，按相处模式与访问阶段（之前、之中、之后）进行分析。

paper.title: Exploring the Paradox of Using Digital Technologies in Nature

works.title: Can't See Nature for the Trees: Virtual Nature for Well-Being
works.description: A systematic review of 124 empirical studies of virtual nature and wellbeing, finding mostly short, passive stress-relief interventions, and proposing four design directions toward cultural, participatory and more-than-human virtual nature.
works.description_zh: 一项对 124 项虚拟自然与身心健康实证研究的系统综述：发现大多是短时、被动的减压干预，并提出四个设计方向，走向文化性、参与性和超越人类视角的虚拟自然。
works.idea_en: Virtual nature need not stop at a calming screensaver; it can host relationships with nature.
works.idea_zh: 虚拟自然不必止于令人放松的屏保，它可以承载与自然的关系。
works.method: PRISMA-style screening of 770 records down to 124 studies, coded for theory, intervention type, duration and outcome.
works.method_zh: 按 PRISMA 流程从 770 条记录筛选出 124 项研究，按理论、干预类型、时长和结果编码。

paper.title: Can’t See Nature for the Trees: A Literature Review about Virtual Nature for Well-Being

works.title: WildCompanion
works.description: An iPhone widget and Apple Watch app that sends people who 'adopted' an endangered animal short, vetted updates and photos about it; a 30-day deployment with 22 adopters showed a calm, steady bond and small conservation actions.
works.description_zh: 一个 iPhone 小组件和 Apple Watch 应用，向“认养”了濒危动物的人推送关于这只动物的简短、经核实的近况和照片；22 位认养者为期 30 天的使用显示出平静而持续的情感联系，以及一些小的保护行动。
works.idea_en: Peripheral, ambient presence can sustain care for a distant wild animal better than one-off immersive media.
works.idea_zh: 边缘的、环境式的存在感，比一次性的沉浸式媒体更能维系对远方野生动物的关心。
works.method: Survey (N=162), interviews (N=18) and co-design with adopters and conservation staff led to the app; 30-day field deployment with logs, weekly questionnaires and exit interviews.
works.method_zh: 经问卷（N=162）、访谈（N=18）以及与认养者和保护机构员工的共同设计形成应用；30 天实地部署，结合日志、每周问卷和结束访谈。

paper.title: Beyond Immersion: Designing Ambient Companions for Wildlife Adoption Engagement

works.title: Nature Engagement Experiences of Blind People
works.description: A survey of blind and sighted people plus in-depth interviews with 16 blind participants about how they experience nature, what keeps them from it, and what assistive technology for nature could look like.
works.description_zh: 一项研究：对盲人和明眼人进行自然关联感问卷，并深度访谈 16 位盲人，了解他们如何体验自然、什么阻碍了他们接近自然，以及面向自然的辅助技术可以是什么样子。
works.idea_en: Nature technology is designed for the eyes; non-visual, safe and meaningful nature access is an open design space.
works.idea_zh: 自然相关的技术大多为眼睛而设计；非视觉、安全而有意义的自然体验，是一片尚待开拓的设计空间。
works.method: Nature Relatedness survey with 20 blind and 20 sighted participants, followed by thematic analysis of interviews.
works.method_zh: 对 20 位盲人和 20 位明眼人进行自然关联感量表调查，再对访谈做主题分析。

paper.title: Understanding Nature Engagement Experiences of Blind People

works.title: Publics, Place, and Sensors: a Community Orchard Sensor Network
works.description: Volunteers at a community orchard co-designed part of a city heat-monitoring sensor network: they decided what it was for, where the sensors went and which data they wanted back.
works.description_zh: 一座社区果园的志愿者共同设计了城市高温监测传感器网络中的一部分：由他们决定网络的用途、传感器放在哪里，以及想要获得哪些数据。
works.idea_en: Environmental sensors become meaningful when placed and read through a community's own practices of tending land.
works.idea_zh: 当传感器的位置和读数都嵌入社区照料土地的日常实践时，环境数据才真正有意义。
works.method: Two participatory design workshops with orchard volunteers, treated as infrastructuring, leading to design criteria for community-driven sensor networks.
works.method_zh: 与果园志愿者举办两场参与式设计工作坊，将其视为“基础设施化”的过程，并由此提出社区驱动传感器网络的设计准则。

paper.title: Publics, Place, and Sensors: Co-Designing Environmental Monitoring with a Community Orchard

works.title: Noondawind
works.description: An environmental data platform co-designed with Ojibwe partners so that Tribal staff and community members can read sensor data and policy resources about Manoomin (wild rice), a sentinel species tied to treaty rights.
works.description_zh: 一个与奥吉布瓦伙伴共同设计的环境数据平台，帮助部落工作人员和社区成员解读有关野生稻（Manoomin）的传感器数据与政策资料；野生稻是与条约权利紧密相关的指示物种。
works.idea_en: Environmental dashboards can be built around an Indigenous relationship with one plant and around data sovereignty.
works.idea_zh: 环境数据平台可以围绕原住民与一种植物的关系、围绕数据主权来构建。
works.method: Iterative participatory design (discover, define, develop, deliver) grounded in Ojibwe worldviews; dashboard connects microclimate sensor data with policy and governance tools.
works.method_zh: 以奥吉布瓦世界观为基础，按发现、定义、开发、交付的迭代参与式设计；平台把微气候传感器数据与政策和治理工具连在一起。

paper.title: Noondawind: Co-Designed Dashboard for Indigenous Data Access and Environmental Policy Implementation

works.title: Makak: Microclimate Sensors for Manoomin (Wild Rice)
works.description: A low-cost floating microclimate sensor co-designed and piloted with four Ojibwe partner organisations to monitor the water and air conditions that affect wild rice beds.
works.description_zh: 一种低成本的漂浮式微气候传感器，与四个奥吉布瓦伙伴机构共同设计并试点，用于监测影响野生稻田的水体和空气条件。
works.idea_en: Conservation sensors can be designed with, and owned by, the people whose culture centres on the species.
works.idea_zh: 保护用的传感器可以由以该物种为文化中心的人们共同设计并拥有。
works.method: Buoy-mounted surface and depth sensors with a BLE mobile app and shared dashboard, developed through a multi-year co-design process with Tribal natural-resource departments (Lac du Flambeau and others).
works.method_zh: 浮标上装有水面与水下传感器，配合蓝牙手机应用和共享数据面板；与部落自然资源部门（Lac du Flambeau 等）经多年共同设计完成。

paper.title: Makak: Co-designing Environmental Sensors to Protect Manoomin (Wild Rice)

works.title: Children's Slow Noticing in Food Gardens
works.description: A study of how 3–5-year-olds notice plants, insects and seasons in childcare food gardens, using prompt cards, an IoT camera and a Bee-Bot robot, leading to design ideas for technology that supports slow noticing.
works.description_zh: 一项关于 3 至 5 岁幼儿如何在托育机构的食物花园中留意植物、昆虫和季节的研究，使用提示卡、物联网相机和 Bee-Bot 机器人，并由此提出支持“慢慢留意”的技术设计方向。
works.idea_en: Design for children's nature connection by supporting three kinds of noticing: focal, relational and temporal.
works.idea_zh: 通过支持三种留意方式——聚焦的、关系的、时间的——来设计儿童与自然的联结。
works.method: Three design activities in childcare centres with cards, a child-operated IoT camera and a programmable floor robot; qualitative analysis of noticing acts.
works.method_zh: 在托育中心开展三项设计活动，使用卡片、儿童可操作的物联网相机和可编程地面机器人，并对留意行为做定性分析。

paper.title: Tuning into Everyday Ecologies: Children’s Slow Noticing in Food Gardens

works.title: The Toronto Water Atlas
works.description: A seven-month design project with artists, scientists and residents that gathered many ways of knowing Toronto's water, from creeks and historical maps to stories and artworks, and kept them side by side rather than reducing water to one planning dataset.
works.description_zh: 一个历时七个月、由艺术家、科学家和居民共同参与的设计项目，汇集了认识多伦多之水的多种方式——从溪流和历史地图到故事与艺术作品——让它们并置，而不是把水简化为一份规划数据。
works.idea_en: Design can stage encounters that keep nature plural, resisting the single definition built into policy informatics.
works.idea_zh: 设计可以搭建相遇的场景，让自然保持多元，抵抗政策信息系统中内置的单一定义。
works.method: Workshops and co-working sessions framed by Mol's ontological multiplicity and Stengers' scene-setting; reflection on design choices that sustain or close down multiple enactments of water.
works.method_zh: 以 Mol 的“本体多重性”和 Stengers 的“布景”概念组织工作坊与共同工作；反思哪些设计选择会维持或关闭水的多重存在方式。

paper.title: The Toronto Water Atlas: Staging Encounters With Nature Through Design

works.title: HCI for Agroecology
works.description: Fieldwork on 11 small UK agroecological farms showing they are poorly served by commercial agri-tech and carry heavy hidden data work, followed by design principles for farmer-led digital tools.
works.description_zh: 在英国 11 个小型农业生态农场开展的田野研究，发现商业农业科技很少适合它们，且农场承担着大量看不见的数据劳动；研究据此提出由农民主导的数字工具设计原则。
works.idea_en: Digital agriculture can be reimagined around grassroots farmer networks and technological sovereignty, not productivity alone.
works.idea_zh: 数字农业可以围绕基层农民网络与技术主权重新设想，而不只是追求产量。
works.method: Ethnographic fieldwork and interviews on farms; analysis of data practices for coordination, planning, monitoring and learning.
works.method_zh: 在农场进行民族志田野调查与访谈，分析协调、计划、监测和学习中的数据实践。

paper.title: HCI for Agroecology: Agri-Tech between Grassroots and Capitalism

works.title: Posthuman / More-than-Human Futures for XR
works.description: A conceptual paper arguing that XR research on space, body and interaction is built on human-centred assumptions, and proposing to reorient them as speculative worlding, distributed decentring and entangled becoming.
works.description_zh: 一篇概念性论文，指出 XR 关于空间、身体与交互的研究建立在以人为中心的假设之上，并提出把它们重新定位为思辨性的造世、分布式的去中心化和纠缠中的生成。
works.idea_en: XR is a medium uniquely suited to more-than-human design, if fidelity and control stop being its default goals.
works.idea_zh: 只要不再把逼真和控制当作默认目标，XR 就是特别适合超越人类设计的媒介。
works.method: Critical review of XR research domains and a co-constitutive framework linking environments, embodiments and enactments.
works.method_zh: 批判性梳理 XR 研究的各个领域，并提出把环境、具身与行动相互关联起来的共构框架。

paper.title: Envisioning Posthuman/More-than-Human Futures for XR through HCI: A Critical Reorientation

works.title: Perch: Seeing with a Bird's Perception
works.description: A sparrow-like wearable robot that sits on the shoulder during a city nature walk and turns birds' patterns of attention into small multimodal cues, nudging the wearer to notice nearby nature.
works.description_zh: 一个像麻雀一样停在肩头的可穿戴机器人，在城市自然漫步中把鸟类的注意模式转化为细微的多模态提示，引导佩戴者留意身边的自然。
works.idea_en: Borrow another species' attention, not its view, as a calm peripheral guide to everyday nature.
works.idea_zh: 借用另一个物种的注意力，而不是它的视野，作为通往日常自然的安静引导。
works.method: Zoomorphic shoulder-worn robot giving subtle multimodal cues (likely movement and sound); mixed-methods study with 18 participants on a nature walk with questionnaires and storyboards.
works.method_zh: 肩戴式仿生机器人，给出细微的多模态提示（很可能是动作和声音）；18 位参与者在自然漫步中使用，并通过问卷和故事板进行混合方法评估。

paper.title: Seeing with a Bird’s Perception: Designing a Wearable Experience to Reorient Attention to Everyday Nature

works.title: InterYard: E-Plants for Attuning to Biorhythms
works.description: A speculative artificial ecosystem of four electronic 'plant species' (E-Ivy, E-Moss, E-Reed, E-Willow) that sense their surroundings and respond with light, inviting city dwellers to follow their rhythms rather than control them.
works.description_zh: 一个思辨性的人工生态系统，由四种电子“植物物种”（E-Ivy、E-Moss、E-Reed、E-Willow）组成，它们感知环境并以光作出回应，邀请城市居民跟随它们的节律而不是控制它们。
works.idea_en: Bio-inspired artificial species can re-teach urban people to live by biological rhythms.
works.idea_zh: 受生物启发的人工物种可以重新教会城市人按生物节律生活。
works.method: Sensor-equipped light objects with fibre-optic 'leaves' that emulate plant behaviours such as light pulses, cyclic colour change and phototropic growth; preliminary study with 12 participants.
works.method_zh: 装有传感器、以光纤为“叶子”的发光物件，模拟植物行为，如光脉冲、周期性变色和向光生长；12 人参与的初步研究。

paper.title: InterYard: Investigating E-Plants as Mediators for Attuning Human to Biorhythms in Future Cities

works.title: Probing More-than-Human Representation in Crisis Resilience Planning
works.description: A workshop in which HCI researchers tried two probes that 'speak for' non-humans in bushfire and flood planning: a voice agent and an immersive XR prototype voicing species such as a gum tree and a platypus.
works.description_zh: 一场工作坊：人机交互研究者试用两种在山火与洪水规划中“替”非人类发声的探针——一个语音代理和一个沉浸式 XR 原型，分别为桉树、鸭嘴兽等物种发声。
works.idea_en: Giving non-humans a voice is not neutral translation: choices of voice, body and realism raise questions of legitimacy and authenticity.
works.idea_zh: 为非人类发声不是中立的翻译：声音、形象与逼真度的选择，都会引出正当性与真实性的问题。
works.method: Scenario-based discussion with an LLM voice agent and an immersive embodied prototype as design probes; thematic analysis.
works.method_zh: 以大语言模型语音代理和沉浸式具身原型作为设计探针，开展情景讨论并做主题分析。

paper.title: Probing More-Than-Human Representation in Crisis Resilience Planning: An HCI Researcher Perspective

works.title: Weathering-With Microclimates
works.description: A portable outdoor workshop in which participants move through shade, vegetation, soil and water, note bodily sensations of heat and relief, fabulate, and then compare what they felt with sensor readings.
works.description_zh: 一种可移植的户外工作坊：参与者穿行于树荫、植被、土壤与水边，记录身体对炎热与舒缓的感受，进行虚构叙事，再把感受与传感器读数对照。
works.idea_en: Treat climate as something we weather with plants, soil and water, sensed through the body before the data.
works.idea_zh: 把气候当作与植物、土壤和水一同经历的东西，先用身体感受，再看数据。
works.method: Guided movement, sketch journals, fabulation and handheld environmental sensing; run as two case studies including architecture students.
works.method_zh: 结合引导式身体活动、速写日志、虚构叙事与手持环境感测；在包括建筑学学生在内的两个案例中实施。

paper.title: Weathering-With Microclimates

works.title: Fermenting Entanglements: Nukabot in the Human–Microbe–AI Triad
works.description: An eight-month deployment of Nukabot, a talking pot of Japanese fermented rice bran, in a science museum and a fermentation shop, where the bot's voice and vocabulary change with the microbes' activity and with the people who tend it.
works.description_zh: Nukabot 是一个会说话的日本米糠腌床（糠床）容器，研究把它在科学馆和发酵专卖店部署了八个月；它的语调和用词会随微生物活动以及照料它的人而变化。
works.idea_en: Some friction in animistic interfaces is useful: it helps people tell the microbes' agency apart from the algorithm's.
works.idea_zh: 拟人化（泛灵）界面中保留一些“摩擦”是有用的：它帮助人分辨哪些是微生物的能动性，哪些是算法的。
works.method: Sensors track the nukadoko's fermentation; a 'Fermenting Design Model' maps metabolic activity and community interaction to voice prosody and vocabulary (likely LLM-generated); studied first in homes (ethics of care) then longitudinally in public sites.
works.method_zh: 传感器追踪糠床的发酵状态；“发酵设计模型”把代谢活动和社群互动映射为语音语调和用词（很可能由大语言模型生成）；先在家庭中（以照料伦理）研究，再在公共场所长期部署。

paper.title: Fermenting Entanglements: Designing for Mutual Care in the Human-Microbe-AI Triad

works.title: Forest Resonance
works.description: A portable transducer that picks up vibrations, the electrical conductivity of bark, moss and soil, and plant bioelectric signals in a forest, and plays them back as sound and touch through wearables; tested with certified forest therapists in Japan.
works.description_zh: 一个便携式换能装置，在森林中采集振动、树皮/苔藓/土壤的导电性以及植物生物电信号，再通过可穿戴设备以声音和触觉回放；在日本与持证森林疗愈师一起进行了测试。
works.idea_en: Make the subtle life of a forest bodily perceptible on site, so walking becomes a practice of noticing.
works.idea_zh: 让森林中细微的生命在现场变得可以用身体感知，使行走成为一种留意的练习。
works.method: Multi-modal contact sensing (vibration, surface conductivity, plant bioelectricity) mapped to sonic–haptic feedback; several interaction modes for moving through the forest; pilot study at a forest therapy base.
works.method_zh: 多模态接触感测（振动、表面导电性、植物生物电）映射为声音与触觉反馈；设计了在森林中移动时的多种交互模式；在森林疗愈基地进行试点研究。

paper.title: Forest Resonance: Sonic–Haptic Interactions Toward In-Situ Engagement with Subtle More-than-Human Life

works.title: Hybrid Nature Crafts
works.description: A pictorial on craft workshops in which 15 children combined leaves and other natural materials with light, showing how making helped them notice nature, make places and build meanings with nature.
works.description_zh: 一篇图文论文，记录 15 名儿童把树叶等自然材料与光结合的手工工作坊，展示制作如何帮助他们留意自然、营造场所，并与自然一起建构意义。
works.idea_en: Children connect with nature when they make with it, not only when technology shows it to them.
works.idea_zh: 儿童在与自然一起制作时，而不只是在技术向他们展示自然时，才真正与自然建立联系。
works.method: Two workshop series in different settings, documenting children's creative processes with hybrid natural–digital materials.
works.method_zh: 在不同场地开展两轮工作坊，记录儿童使用自然与数字混合材料的创作过程。

paper.title: Children's Creative Engagement in Hybrid Nature Crafting: Materiality Meaning and Connection

works.title: Hike Your Own Hike: Noticing Through Iterative Physical Disorientation
works.description: A retrospective autoethnography of hiking and backpacking showing that gear, apps, waymarks and the trail itself frame nature as separate from people, while weather, vast landscapes and fragile bodies keep forcing hikers to notice the more-than-human.
works.description_zh: 一项关于徒步与背包旅行的回顾性自我民族志：装备、应用、路标乃至步道本身都把自然框定为与人分离的东西，而天气、广阔的地景和脆弱的身体却不断迫使徒步者留意超越人类的世界。
works.idea_en: Repeated disorientation outdoors can be a design-relevant method for decentring the human.
works.idea_zh: 在户外一次次的迷失，可以成为一种与设计相关、让人从中心退开的方法。
works.method: First-person retrospective autoethnography across multiple hikes, using disorientation as a methodological lens.
works.method_zh: 以“迷失”为方法透镜，对多次徒步进行第一人称回顾性自我民族志。

paper.title: Hike Your Own Hike: Noticing Through Iterative Physical Disorientation

works.title: Biophilic Interaction in Indoor Environments
works.description: A design framework, built from sessions with architects, that translates qualities of natural phenomena, beyond visual greenery, into ways people interact with indoor environments.
works.description_zh: 一个基于与建筑师共同设计工作的设计框架，把视觉绿化之外的自然现象特质，转化为人与室内环境的交互方式。
works.idea_en: Biophilia indoors can be an interaction quality, not just greenery to look at.
works.idea_zh: 室内的亲生物性可以是一种交互品质，而不只是供人观看的绿色植物。
works.method: Design sessions with architects distilled into seven biophilic dimensions, seven design values and six interaction forms; builds on the authors' DIS 2025 study of multisensory biophilic futures.
works.method_zh: 通过与建筑师的设计工作，提炼出七个亲生物维度、七项设计价值和六种交互形式；延续作者在 DIS 2025 关于多感官亲生物未来的研究。

paper.title: Biophilic Interaction in Indoor Environments: A Design Framework

works.title: SymbioSip
works.description: A two-way hydration wearable: when the wearer is dehydrated a pump waters their houseplant, and when the plant's soil dries out a fine mist sprays the wearer's head.
works.description_zh: 一个双向补水的可穿戴装置：佩戴者缺水时，水泵会给家中的盆栽浇水；植物土壤变干时，一阵细雾会喷到佩戴者头上。
works.idea_en: Couple a person's and a plant's needs in both directions so caring for one reminds you of the other.
works.idea_zh: 把人和植物的需求双向耦合，照顾其中一方就会想起另一方。
works.method: Wearable dehydration sensing triggers a plant irrigation pump; a soil-moisture sensor triggers a head-worn mist sprayer.
works.method_zh: 可穿戴的脱水感测触发植物浇水泵；土壤湿度传感器触发头戴式喷雾器。

paper.title: SymbioSip: Human-Plant Symbiosis through a Bidirectional Hydration System

works.title: Making SeaFoam
works.description: A pictorial following a designer who gathered washed-up seaweed and oyster shells, extracted agar in a kitchen lab and made SeaFoam, a biomaterial for interactive artefacts, as a way of getting to know local coastal ecologies.
works.description_zh: 一篇图文论文：设计者收集被冲上岸的海藻和牡蛎壳，在厨房实验室里提取琼脂，制成用于交互作品的生物材料 SeaFoam，以此了解当地的海岸生态。
works.idea_en: Making a material from what the sea casts ashore can be a method of noticing, not just of sourcing.
works.idea_zh: 用大海冲上岸的东西制作材料，可以是一种留意的方法，而不只是获取原料。
works.method: DIY agar extraction from seaweed, oyster-shell powder for texture, autobiographical research-through-design journaling combined with material-driven design.
works.method_zh: 自制海藻琼脂提取，加入牡蛎壳粉调节质感；结合自传式设计研究日志与材料驱动设计方法。

paper.title: Making Seafoam: An Autobiographical Design Journey Engaging Local Ecologies Through Making

works.title: Habitabilities of Bacterial Cellulose for Living Artefacts
works.description: A visual account of lab work showing that bacterial cellulose (the kombucha 'SCOBY' mat) can be a home for fungi, microalgae and cyanobacteria, with options for tuning it to host other organisms in living artefacts.
works.description_zh: 一篇以图像叙述实验室工作的论文：细菌纤维素（康普茶“红茶菌”膜）可以成为真菌、微藻和蓝藻的栖所，并给出调节它以容纳其他生物、用于“活的人造物”的多种方法。
works.idea_en: Treat a grown material not only as a substitute for plastic but as a habitat other species can live in.
works.idea_zh: 不只把生长出来的材料当作塑料的替代品，而是当作其他物种可以居住的栖所。
works.method: Hands-on biolab experiments with Komagataeibacter and co-inhabiting organisms, documented through visual storytelling.
works.method_zh: 以 Komagataeibacter 及共栖生物进行实验室动手实验，并用视觉叙事记录。

paper.title: On the Habitabilities of Bacterial Cellulose for Living Artefacts

works.title: (Un)-blanketing Indigenous Climate Change Indicators
works.description: A pictorial on the Indigenous Climate Observatories project in Eswatini, Lesotho and Sarawak, where each community conversation started on a blanket and ended in a hand-made blanket recording local signs of climate change.
works.description_zh: 一篇关于“原住民气候观测站”项目的图文论文，项目在埃斯瓦蒂尼、莱索托和砂拉越开展：每次社区对话都从一张毯子开始，最后形成一张记录当地气候变化迹象的手工毯子。
works.idea_en: A shared blanket can serve as both meeting place and boundary object for weaving Indigenous and scientific climate knowledge.
works.idea_zh: 一张共享的毯子，既可以是聚会的场所，也可以是编织原住民知识与科学气候知识的边界物。
works.method: Two years of participatory work with local researchers, Indigenous communities and a meteorological service, using blankets as design seeds and records.
works.method_zh: 与当地研究者、原住民社区和气象部门开展两年的参与式工作，以毯子作为设计种子和记录载体。

paper.title: (Un)-blanketing Indigenous Climate Change Indicators for Understanding Local Climate Change

works.title: Rewilding Human Life: Seasonal Crafts with Children
works.description: An annotated portfolio of forty seasonal nature crafts done over a year at home and outdoors with family, friends and neighbours, following a Swedish children's book of nature experiments, to cultivate wonder and care.
works.description_zh: 一份带注释的作品集：依照一本瑞典儿童自然实验书，在一年中与家人、朋友和邻居在家中和户外完成四十项季节性自然手工，以培养惊奇感与照料之心。
works.idea_en: Frivolous, seasonal crafts with children are a practice of 'rewilding human life' that more-than-human design should include.
works.idea_zh: 与孩子一起做的、看似无用的季节手工，是一种“让人的生活重新野化”的实践，超越人类的设计应当把它纳入。
works.method: First-person annotated portfolio arranged as a visual calendar, with reflection on technology, frivolity and children's place in ecological care.
works.method_zh: 以视觉日历形式整理的第一人称注释作品集，并反思技术、无用之趣以及儿童在生态照料中的位置。

paper.title: Rewilding Human Life: An Annotated Portfolio of Seasonal Crafts with Children

works.title: Embroidered Geographies
works.description: Seven GIS-generated maps of a seven-day bike trip down the Mississippi River, hand-embroidered over 18 months as a way of thinking about rivers, data and more-than-human entanglement.
works.description_zh: 把一次为期七天、沿密西西比河骑行的旅程生成为七张 GIS 地图，再用 18 个月手工刺绣出来，以此思考河流、数据与超越人类的纠缠。
works.idea_en: Slow embroidery over GPS maps undoes the Cartesian view of a river and lets its time and body back in.
works.idea_zh: 在 GPS 地图上缓慢刺绣，能拆解对河流的笛卡尔式表达，让河流的时间与身体重新进入。
works.method: Autoethnographic bike tour logged with GPS, maps produced in GIS, then embroidered by hand; reflective vignettes on embroidery as feminist epistemology.
works.method_zh: 自我民族志式骑行并以 GPS 记录，用 GIS 生成地图后手工刺绣；以反思片段讨论刺绣作为女性主义认识论。

paper.title: Stitching Together Body, Land, and Data through Embroidered Geographies

works.title: Entangled Histories Radio
works.description: A vintage radio that plays speeches and music from the American Civil Rights Movement, selected by real-time readings from sensors at the base of an urban tree, treating the city forest as a 'living archive' entwined with a human one.
works.description_zh: 一台老式收音机，播放美国民权运动的演讲与音乐；播放内容由城市树木根部传感器的实时读数选择，把城市森林当作与人类档案相互交织的“活档案”。
works.idea_en: More-than-human design can hold socio-political history too: let a tree's living conditions voice the struggles that shaped its city.
works.idea_zh: 超越人类的设计也可以承载社会政治历史：让一棵树的生存状态说出塑造这座城市的抗争。
works.method: ESP32 with rain, soil-moisture, sound and BME680 environmental sensors at a tree base maps ecological inputs onto a curated audio archive played through a vintage radio; work in progress.
works.method_zh: 树根处的 ESP32 连接雨量、土壤湿度、声音和 BME680 环境传感器，把生态数据映射到精选的音频档案，并通过老式收音机播放；仍在进行中的研究。

paper.title: Entangled Histories Radio: Exploring Ecological Justice and Civil Rights Through Tangible Interactions

works.title: Sketching More-than-human Times
works.description: A pictorial on designing the More-than-Human Temporal Ontologies booklet, a tool of sketches and prompts for embodied, entangled and deep time that helps researchers talk about time beyond clock and calendar.
works.description_zh: 一篇关于设计《超越人类的时间本体》小册子的图文论文：这本小册子用速写和提示，呈现具身的、纠缠的和深时尺度的时间，帮助研究者讨论钟表和日历之外的时间。
works.idea_en: How we draw time shapes what we design; a booklet of alternative time drawings can open that up.
works.idea_zh: 我们如何画时间，决定了我们设计什么；一本另类时间图示的小册子可以打开这一点。
works.method: Critique of Western industrial time representations, followed by embodied sketching and imagining of multiple more-than-human temporalities compiled into a booklet.
works.method_zh: 先批判西方工业化的时间表达，再通过具身速写与想象呈现多种超越人类的时间性，汇编成册。

paper.title: Sketching More-than-human Times: Rethinking Temporal Representations through Embodied, Entangled, and Deep time

works.title: Staying with the Underwater Trouble: Freediving the Hydrocommons
works.description: A pictorial that uses the author's own freediving, underwater photography and micro-phenomenological reflection to explore breath-hold immersion as a way of sensing one's body as continuous with the ocean.
works.description_zh: 一篇图文论文：作者以自己的自由潜水、水下摄影和微观现象学反思，探索屏气潜入水中如何让人感到身体与海洋相连。
works.idea_en: Breathwork and immersion can be a design research method for transcorporeal connection with water.
works.idea_zh: 呼吸练习与身体浸入，可以成为与水建立“跨身体”联系的设计研究方法。
works.method: Autoethnographic freediving practice documented through underwater photography and micro-phenomenological interviews.
works.method_zh: 以水下摄影和微观现象学访谈记录的自我民族志自由潜水实践。

paper.title: Staying with the Underwater Trouble: Exploring the Hydrocommons through Freediving.

works.title: Drawing Attention: From Observational Sketching to Noticing
works.description: A set of reflection prompts that turn observational sketching into a noticing practice for more-than-human design, developed in a four-month residency and tried with nine participants.
works.description_zh: 一套把观察性速写变成超越人类设计中“留意”练习的反思提示，在四个月的驻留中发展出来，并由九位参与者试用。
works.idea_en: Reflecting on your own sketch (what you chose, what the medium did, what you left out) reveals blind spots that prompt further noticing.
works.idea_zh: 反思自己的速写——选择了什么、媒介起了什么作用、遗漏了什么——会暴露盲点，从而促使进一步的留意。
works.method: First-person sketching residency yielding scaffolding elements, then guided sketching and reflection sessions with participants; offered as a tool for multispecies ethnography.
works.method_zh: 第一人称速写驻留产生一组引导要素，再与参与者进行引导式速写与反思；作为多物种民族志的工具。

paper.title: Drawing Attention: From Observational Sketching to Noticing

works.title: An Otter Delight: Speculative Design for Outdoor Recreation Technology
works.description: Speculative redesigns of surf and outdoor recreation apps built around Otter 841, the Santa Cruz sea otter known for taking surfboards, asking how such apps could steer people toward the needs of wildlife they share the water with.
works.description_zh: 围绕圣克鲁兹以“抢冲浪板”闻名的 841 号海獭，对冲浪与户外休闲应用进行思辨性再设计，追问这类应用如何把人引向与之共享水域的野生动物的需要。
works.idea_en: Recreation apps that guide people into nature could also guide them to share it, using commons theory as a design lens.
works.idea_zh: 把人引入自然的休闲应用，也可以引导人们分享自然；可以把公地理论当作设计透镜。
works.method: Speculative design grounded in conservation research and Ostrom's and Hardin's work on the commons, centred on one individual animal.
works.method_zh: 以保护研究以及 Ostrom 和 Hardin 关于公地的理论为基础的思辨设计，以一只具体的动物为中心。

paper.title: An Otter Delight- Using Speculative Design for Long-Term Sustainable Engagements through Outdoor Recreation Technologies

works.title: Accessing Posthuman Concepts: RoPPi, Critter Connect and ChatSpecies
works.description: Three interactive artefacts for science communication beyond the human: RoPPi, a storytelling game from nonhuman perspectives; Critter Connect, a haptic interface for sensing nonhuman presence; and ChatSpecies, an AI agent for talking with museum specimens. Shown to 23 science communicators.
works.description_zh: 三件面向超越人类视角的科学传播交互作品：RoPPi，一个以非人类视角讲故事的游戏；Critter Connect，一个感受非人类存在的触觉界面；ChatSpecies，一个可以与博物馆标本对话的 AI 代理。研究向 23 位科学传播从业者展示并收集反馈。
works.idea_en: Interactive artefacts can work as epistemic technologies that let the public try out posthuman ideas.
works.idea_zh: 交互作品可以作为“认识论技术”，让公众亲身尝试后人类的观念。
works.method: Presentation of three prototypes at the SciComPt 2025 congress with reflections from practitioners analysed qualitatively.
works.method_zh: 在 SciComPt 2025 大会上展示三个原型，并对从业者的反思做定性分析。

paper.title: Accessing Posthuman Concepts: Epistemic Technologies for Public Engagement Beyond the Human

works.title: Towards Multispecies Participation in More-than-human Worlds
works.description: A positioning paper from the PDC 2026 conversation 'Post-anthropocentrism and Participation: Multispecies', gathering cases and critiques on who and what can take part in participatory design across species lines.
works.description_zh: 一篇立场论文，来自 PDC 2026 的对话环节“后人类中心与参与：多物种”，汇集了关于跨物种参与式设计中“谁和什么可以参与”的案例与批评。
works.idea_en: Participatory design can be reconfigured around relationality, care, response-ability and not-knowing so that other species take part.
works.idea_zh: 参与式设计可以围绕关系性、照料、回应能力和“不知道”来重构，使其他物种也能参与其中。
works.method: Synthesis of applied cases, critical perspectives and exploratory approaches presented at the conference conversation.
works.method_zh: 综合会议对话中呈现的应用案例、批判视角和探索性方法。

paper.title: Towards Multispecies Participation in More-than-human Worlds

works.title: Bio-Inclusive Design: From Control to Co-Evolution
works.description: A paper that brings participatory design to living materials, using a bacterial cellulose case to ask how living matter can be treated as an active stakeholder in the design process.
works.description_zh: 一篇把参与式设计引入活体材料的论文，以细菌纤维素为案例，探讨如何把活的物质当作设计过程中的主动利益相关者。
works.idea_en: When materials are alive, the designer's role shifts from controller to facilitator of a dialogue with them.
works.idea_zh: 当材料是活的，设计者的角色就从控制者转变为与材料对话的促成者。
works.method: Critical literature analysis plus a bacterial cellulose case study, examining ethical, epistemological and operational challenges.
works.method_zh: 批判性文献分析加细菌纤维素案例研究，考察伦理、认识论与操作层面的挑战。

paper.title: From Control to Co-Evolution: Rethinking Participation in Bio-Inclusive Design

works.title: Hizca
works.description: A video game co-created with the Muisca Indigenous community of Sesquilé and a design team in Bogotá about the Colombian páramo, the high-Andean ecosystem that supplies much of the region's water, and the threats it faces.
works.description_zh: 一款与塞斯基莱的穆伊斯卡原住民社区和波哥大设计团队共同创作的电子游戏，讲述哥伦比亚帕拉莫高原——为该地区提供大量水源的安第斯高山生态系统——以及它所面临的威胁。
works.idea_en: A game can carry Indigenous ecological knowledge in its mechanics and aesthetics, not just its story.
works.idea_zh: 游戏可以在机制与美学中、而不只是在故事里，承载原住民的生态知识。
works.method: Three-phase participatory method (Conceptualization, Translation, Verification) braiding community knowledge into narrative, mechanics and art.
works.method_zh: 三阶段参与式方法（概念化、转译、验证），把社区知识编入叙事、机制与美术。

paper.title: Hizca, a Critical Video Game and Indigenous Co-creation.: Defending the Colombian Pãramo and Imagining Sustainable Futures

works.title: Mediating More-Than-Human Encounters Across Spatio-Temporal Distance
works.description: A critical reflection on three human–computer–biosphere interaction designs that bring remote, slow or tiny ecosystems into view, asking when such mediation brings people closer and when it adds new distance.
works.description_zh: 对三项“人-计算机-生物圈交互”设计的批判性反思：这些设计让遥远、缓慢或微小的生态系统进入视野，研究追问这种中介何时拉近距离、何时反而造成新的距离。
works.idea_en: Mediating nature at a distance creates its own tensions of temporal mismatch and authenticity; social mediation can ease them.
works.idea_zh: 远程中介自然会带来时间错位与真实性的张力；社会性的中介可以缓解这些张力。
works.method: Research-through-design reflection across three public-facing works, analysing psychological distances, tensions and engagement.
works.method_zh: 对三件面向公众的作品进行设计研究式反思，分析心理距离、张力与参与情况。

paper.title: Mediating More-Than-Human Encounters Across Spatio-Temporal Distance

works.title: Technology for Joyful and Caring Human–Forest Interactions
works.description: Reflections from a one-week summer school in the Pre-Pyrenees where participants spent time in the forest and speculated on technologies in which joy and care for the forest reinforce each other, yielding four design qualities.
works.description_zh: 来自比利牛斯山前一周暑期学校的反思：参与者在森林中度过时光，并思辨哪些技术能让对森林的喜悦与照料相互促进，由此提出四项设计品质。
works.idea_en: Joy in the forest and care for the forest can be designed together rather than traded off.
works.idea_zh: 在森林中的喜悦与对森林的照料，可以一起设计，而不必此消彼长。
works.method: Collaborative inquiry in the forest (time outdoors, shared stories, speculative making) with reflexive thematic analysis.
works.method_zh: 在森林中的协作探究（户外时光、分享经历、思辨制作），并进行反思性主题分析。

paper.title: How Can We Design Technology for Joyful and Caring Human-Forest Interactions?: Ideas and Reflections from a One-Week Summer School in the Pre-Pyrenees Mountains

works.title: Non-Human Persona Perception Scale (NH-PPS)
works.description: A modified questionnaire for evaluating non-human personas, which designers increasingly use to give animals, plants or ecosystems a 'voice', replacing constructs that assume human social norms.
works.description_zh: 一份用于评估非人类人物角色的改编问卷；设计者越来越多地用这类角色为动物、植物或生态系统“发声”，问卷替换了原量表中预设人类社会规范的维度。
works.idea_en: If we design non-human personas, we need ways to judge them that are not borrowed from human psychology.
works.idea_zh: 既然我们在设计非人类角色，就需要不借用人类心理学的评判方式。
works.method: Conceptual analysis and expert review to derive constructs and candidate items; formative evaluation with 24 participants using two non-human personas.
works.method_zh: 通过概念分析和专家评审得出维度与候选题项；以两个非人类角色、24 位参与者进行形成性评估。

paper.title: Reconceptualizing the Persona Perception Scale for Non-Human Personas: A Formative Validation Study

works.title: The Illusion of the Posthuman Turn in HCI
works.description: A provocation arguing that HCI's 'posthuman turn' often adopts the vocabulary of entanglement while keeping humanist assumptions about knowledge, method and value, and offering a simple test for when posthuman commitments are actually enacted.
works.description_zh: 一篇挑战性文章，认为人机交互的“后人类转向”常常只借用“纠缠”等词汇，却保留了关于知识、方法与价值的人文主义假设，并提出一个判断后人类承诺是否真正落实的简单框架。
works.idea_en: Posthuman design needs alignment across ontology, epistemology, method and ethics, not just new words.
works.idea_zh: 后人类设计需要本体论、认识论、方法与伦理的一致，而不只是新的词汇。
works.method: Theoretical critique drawing on critical posthumanism, new materialism and feminist epistemologies; proposes research through design as suited to immanence.
works.method_zh: 借助批判后人类主义、新物质主义与女性主义认识论进行理论批评；提出设计研究（RtD）适合在内在性条件下运作。

paper.title: The Illusion of the Posthuman Turn in HCI

works.title: Design Tropes of More Than Human Confusion
works.description: A critique paper naming three recurring tropes in interaction design, speculative design and media art (The Tortured Plant, The Cyberpunk Wearable and The Faked Human) and showing how each plays with the boundaries of human, non-human and machine agency.
works.description_zh: 一篇批评性论文，归纳交互设计、思辨设计和媒体艺术中反复出现的三种套路——“受折磨的植物”“赛博朋克可穿戴”和“伪装的人”——并说明它们如何玩弄人、非人与机器能动性之间的边界。
works.idea_en: Confusion about who acts in a more-than-human design can be a critical tool, if designers recognise the trope they are using.
works.idea_zh: 如果设计者意识到自己在用哪种套路，那么关于“谁在行动”的混乱本身就可以成为一种批判工具。
works.method: Critical analysis of recognised design projects and artworks grouped into tropes; complements the author's CHI 2026 essay on the pre-millennial roots of posthumanism in interaction design.
works.method_zh: 对知名设计项目与艺术作品进行批判性分析并归纳成套路；与作者在 CHI 2026 发表的关于交互设计中后人类主义早期根源的文章互为补充。

paper.title: Design Tropes of More Than Human Confusion

works.title: CHORALE: More-Than-Human Consent in Reef Ecologies
works.description: A speculative installation of distributed AI nodes in which visitors take the roles of reef organisms and communicate through sound, light and body movement, exploring consent as something coral and other reef life could give, withhold or revoke.
works.description_zh: 一件由分布式 AI 节点组成的思辨装置：观众扮演珊瑚礁中的生物，通过声音、光和身体动作交流，探讨“同意”如何成为珊瑚等礁区生命可以给予、拒绝或撤回的东西。
works.idea_en: Instead of AI that monitors reefs as data, imagine AI that mediates consent: embodied, ongoing and revocable.
works.idea_zh: 与其让 AI 把珊瑚礁当作数据来监测，不如设想一种协调“同意”的 AI：具身的、持续的、可撤回的。
works.method: Interactive fabulation with networked AI nodes responding to sound, light and bodily interaction; developed by students in Elisa Giaccardi's group at Politecnico di Milano.
works.method_zh: 以联网 AI 节点构成的交互虚构作品，响应声音、光与身体互动；由米兰理工大学 Elisa Giaccardi 团队的学生开发。

paper.title: CHORALE: A Speculative Interactive Installation for More-Than-Human Consent in Reef Ecologies

works.title: Charismatic Data: Monitoring Bird–Building Collisions
works.description: An account of Safe Flight volunteers in the US South who walk routes to find birds killed by striking buildings, log them in an app, record their own effort and collect the bodies for university specimen collections, to push for bird-safe building rules.
works.description_zh: 记录美国南部 Safe Flight 志愿者的工作：他们沿固定路线寻找撞上建筑而死的鸟，在应用中登记、记录自己的巡查工作，并把鸟的尸体收集送往大学标本馆，以推动鸟类友好建筑法规。
works.idea_en: Citizen-science data gains advocacy power when paired with material traces such as the birds' bodies themselves.
works.idea_zh: 当公民科学数据与实物痕迹（例如鸟的遗体）相结合，它就获得了倡导的力量。
works.method: Ethnographic study of volunteer monitoring producing three data forms: a digital strike record, an effort log and a specimen collection.
works.method_zh: 对志愿者监测的民族志研究，涉及三种数据形式：数字撞击记录、巡查工作日志和标本收藏。

paper.title: Charismatic Data and Material Traces: Monitoring Bird-Building Collisions through Citizen Science

works.title: An Archive of Tensions in More-Than-Human Design
works.description: An Interactions forum article presenting a growing, crowd-sourced collection of tensions designers face in more-than-human design (such as anthropomorphism, decentring and good intentions with harmful effects), mapped and open to new contributions.
works.description_zh: 一篇《Interactions》论坛文章，介绍一个持续增长、众包而成的“张力档案”，收集设计者在超越人类设计中遇到的张力（如拟人化、去中心化、好意却带来负面后果），并以图谱呈现、欢迎新的贡献。
works.idea_en: Collect and map the recurring dilemmas of more-than-human design so practitioners can see and discuss them openly.
works.idea_zh: 收集并绘制超越人类设计中反复出现的两难，让从业者能公开看见并讨论它们。
works.method: Tensions gathered (likely from workshops and the authors' own projects), organised into a map linking design, theory and world; readers can add cases via a QR-linked archive.
works.method_zh: 收集张力（很可能来自工作坊和作者自己的项目），整理成连接设计、理论与世界的图谱；读者可通过二维码链接的档案添加案例。

paper.title: An Archive of Tensions: A Growing Collection of Challenges in More-Than-Human Design

works.title: The More-than-Human Talking Stick
works.description: An artefact for a permaculture garden community that brings a more-than-human voice into mostly human conversations, designed from three principles (consideration, connectedness, dynamics) drawn from fieldwork in the garden.
works.description_zh: 一件为朴门（永续农业）花园社区设计的物件，把超越人类的声音带入以人为主的对话；其设计依据来自花园田野工作的三项原则：体察、联结与动态。
works.idea_en: Borrow the talking stick, a tool for whose turn it is to speak, and give a turn to the garden itself.
works.idea_zh: 借用“发言杖”这一决定轮到谁说话的工具，把发言的机会也交给花园本身。
works.method: Fieldwork at a permaculture garden community analysed into design principles that guided the artefact and ongoing awareness of multispecies agency.
works.method_zh: 在朴门花园社区进行田野调查，提炼出设计原则，用以指导物件设计并持续提醒人们关注多物种的能动性。

paper.title: The More-than-Human Talking Stick: Design Principles for Multispecies Entanglement and Agency

works.title: Becoming Humus
works.description: Two public workshops in which participants made phosphate fertiliser from their own urine, linking their bodies to the planetary phosphorus cycle and reframing urine from taboo to resource.
works.description_zh: 两场公共工作坊：参与者用自己的尿液制作磷肥，把身体与行星尺度的磷循环联系起来，让尿液从禁忌变成资源。
works.idea_en: Ecological literacy can start inside the body: making fertiliser from yourself makes 'humans as humus' tangible.
works.idea_zh: 生态素养可以从身体内部开始：用自己制作肥料，让“人即腐殖质”变得可以触摸。
works.method: Experiential pedagogy drawing on Haraway, Braidotti and the Planetary Boundaries framework; participants recover phosphate from urine (likely via precipitation) and reflect on bodily and planetary metabolisms.
works.method_zh: 借鉴 Haraway、Braidotti 与“行星边界”框架的体验式教学；参与者从尿液中回收磷酸盐（很可能通过沉淀法），并反思身体与行星的新陈代谢。

paper.title: Becoming humus: Embodied ecological literacy through designing

works.title: Kin Bank
works.description: A speculative interface modelled on a shared bank account, which uses synthetic data to generate poetic 'transactions' between city residents and the non-human actors whose data smart-city systems leave out.
works.description_zh: 一个以“共享银行账户”为原型的思辨界面，用合成数据生成城市居民与非人类行动者之间诗意的“交易记录”，这些非人类的数据正是智慧城市系统所遗漏的。
works.idea_en: When real data on non-humans is missing, synthetic data can be used not to predict but to provoke: 'productive uncertainty'.
works.idea_zh: 当关于非人类的真实数据缺失时，合成数据可以不用于预测，而用于激发思考，制造“有益的不确定性”。
works.method: Research through design of a banking-style interface populated with generated ecological–financial interdependencies; user study on reflection and perceived relationships.
works.method_zh: 以设计研究方式开发银行式界面，填充生成的生态-金融相互依存记录；并进行关于反思与关系感知的用户研究。

paper.title: Speculative Design Through Synthetic Data: Exploring how synthetic data be used to represent missing ‘more-than-human' data

works.title: From Decoration to Co-Presence: Office Plants with Aesthetic Biofeedback
works.description: A biofeedback artefact that expresses an office plant's vitality through light and sound, deployed long-term in workplaces; employees described empathy and companionship, but also guilt and resistance when the plant demanded attention.
works.description_zh: 一个通过光和声音表达办公室植物生命状态的生物反馈装置，在职场中长期部署；员工描述了共情与陪伴感，也描述了植物“要求”关注时的内疚与抗拒。
works.idea_en: Making a plant perceptible turns it from décor into a co-worker, and brings the ethics of care into office routines.
works.idea_zh: 让植物变得可被感知，就把它从装饰变成了“同事”，也把照料的伦理带进了办公室日常。
works.method: Research through design: interviews, an aesthetic biofeedback artefact sensing plant state (likely soil moisture and light) and a longitudinal workplace deployment.
works.method_zh: 设计研究：访谈、一个感知植物状态（很可能是土壤湿度和光照）的审美生物反馈装置，以及在职场中的长期部署。

paper.title: From Decoration to Co-Presence: Reconfiguring Human–Plant Relations in Urban Workplaces Through Aesthetic Bio-Feedback

works.title: Careful Configurations
works.description: A series of eco-social prototypes, from modular heating and communal hydration to wooden fridges and moss bathrooms, proposed as 'careful' rather than 'smart' technologies that take part in human–material–environment relations.
works.description_zh: 一系列生态-社会原型，从模块化供暖、共享饮水到木制冰箱和苔藓浴室，被提出作为“细心的”而非“智能的”技术，参与人、材料与环境之间的关系。
works.idea_en: Replace 'smart' with 'careful': judge innovations by care and resourcefulness, recasting feasibility, viability and desirability as relational.
works.idea_zh: 用“细心”取代“智能”：以照料与就地取材的能力衡量创新，把可行性、可持续性与合意性重新理解为关系性的能力。
works.method: Prototype series analysed through Barad's intra-action; proposes a care-based model of design innovation.
works.method_zh: 以 Barad 的“内在作用”（intra-action）概念分析一系列原型，并提出以照料为基础的设计创新模式。

paper.title: Careful Configurations: An Exploration of Smart Technologies in More-Than-Human Innovation

works.title: Play and Pilina: Bio-Collaborative Play
works.description: Introduces bio-collaborative play, in which plants, microbes and everyday materials are treated as kin and co-authors of play worlds, grounded in the Native Hawaiian principles of pilina (reciprocal care) and kuleana (responsibility).
works.description_zh: 提出“生物协作游戏”：把植物、微生物和日常材料视为亲族与游戏世界的共同作者，并以夏威夷原住民的 pilina（互惠照料）与 kuleana（责任）原则为根基。
works.idea_en: Let materials grow, decay and respond during play, and play becomes reciprocal stewardship.
works.idea_zh: 在游戏中允许材料生长、腐烂和回应，游戏就成了互惠的守护。
works.method: Practice-based play design and workshops combining consumer materials with place-based natural matter and living organisms.
works.method_zh: 以实践为基础的游戏设计与工作坊，把日常消费材料与在地自然物和活的生物结合起来。

paper.title: Play and Pilina: Reimagining Play Design Through Material Kinship and Cultural Practice

works.title: Cuia Colab: Design Across Species, Worlds and Relations
works.description: A design research project with traditional cuia artisans in Santarém (Brazilian Amazon), combining fieldwork, biodesign experiments with the living calabash tree's fruit and a co-created exhibition, to test whether biodesign can create fair exchanges with traditional knowledge.
works.description_zh: 一个与巴西亚马孙圣塔伦传统葫芦碗（cuia）工匠合作的设计研究项目，结合田野调查、以葫芦树活果实进行的生物设计实验和共同策划的展览，检验生物设计能否与传统知识建立公平的交换。
works.idea_en: Biodesign in the Amazon must align the interests of artisans, trees and designers, overcoming hierarchies of knowledge.
works.idea_zh: 亚马孙的生物设计必须协调工匠、树和设计者的利益，克服知识之间的等级。
works.method: Literature review, case study of Santarém cuias, participant observation with artisans, biodesign experiments with living organisms (likely shaping Crescentia cujete fruits as they grow on the tree), and a co-created exhibition.
works.method_zh: 文献综述、圣塔伦葫芦碗案例研究、与工匠的参与式观察、结合活体生物的生物设计实验（很可能是在葫芦树 Crescentia cujete 果实生长时为其塑形），以及共同策划的展览。

paper.title: Cuia Colab: Toward a Design Across Species, Worlds and Relations

works.title: Biodiverse Walls and the Ethics of Bioempathy
works.description: Biodiverse wall prototypes for buildings, analysed through 'bioempathy' (recognising the intrinsic value of the biotic community), with observations of which plants established and which arrived on their own.
works.description_zh: 为建筑设计的生物多样性墙体原型，以“生物共情”（承认生物群落的内在价值）为框架分析，并观察哪些植物成功定植、哪些自行到来。
works.idea_en: Spontaneous colonisation of a designed wall is feedback: living systems revise the designer's ecological intentions.
works.idea_zh: 生物自发定居在设计好的墙上，本身就是反馈：生命系统会修正设计者的生态意图。
works.method: Ethical-operational framework applied to interdisciplinary wall prototypes; monitoring of plant establishment and spontaneous colonisation.
works.method_zh: 把伦理-操作框架应用于跨学科的墙体原型；监测植物定植与自发定居情况。

paper.title: Biodiverse Design and the Ethics of Bioempathy in Practice

works.title: A Common Language for More-than-Human Representation Tools
works.description: Workshops with 12 more-than-human design researchers testing a set of parameters for choosing, designing and evaluating tools that represent non-humans (personas, probes, simulations); the parameters worked as decision aids, reflection lenses and a shared vocabulary.
works.description_zh: 与 12 位超越人类设计研究者开展工作坊，检验一组用于选择、设计和评估“非人类表征工具”（人物角色、探针、模拟等）的参数；这些参数被用作决策辅助、反思透镜和共同语言。
works.idea_en: Representation tools for non-humans need a shared vocabulary of trade-offs, used as flexible frames rather than checklists.
works.idea_zh: 表征非人类的工具需要一套关于取舍的共同语言，它应作为灵活的参照框架而非检查清单。
works.method: Workshop study applying parameters proposed in the authors' DIS 2025 paper to participants' own tools.
works.method_zh: 工作坊研究，把作者在 DIS 2025 论文中提出的参数应用到参与者自己的工具上。

paper.title: Towards a common language for representation tools in more-than-human design

works.title: Monsters of Marine Debris
works.description: A workshop kit that turns citizen-science data on beach and marine litter into 'monsters', using futures scaffolding so participants imagine ocean futures rather than only count debris.
works.description_zh: 一套工作坊工具包，把关于海滩与海洋垃圾的公民科学数据变成“怪兽”，借助“未来支架”方法，让参与者想象海洋的未来，而不只是统计垃圾。
works.idea_en: Citizen data can be a generative design material for affective, imaginative engagement, not just objective counting.
works.idea_zh: 公民数据可以成为一种生成性的设计材料，用于情感和想象的投入，而不只是客观统计。
works.method: Co-speculative design kit applied in workshops; framed as 'futures scaffolding' for embedded, embodied and emergent thinking.
works.method_zh: 在工作坊中使用的共同思辨设计工具包；以“未来支架”方法支持嵌入式、具身和涌现式的思考。

paper.title: Scaffolding Oceans Futures: Design for embedded, embodied, and emergent thinking

works.title: Teaching More-than-Human Perspectives in Technology Design
works.description: A collection of practical classroom activities, organised in a framework, that design teachers can use to introduce students to more-than-human perspectives in technology design.
works.description_zh: 一套按框架整理的实用课堂活动，设计教师可用来向学生介绍技术设计中的超越人类视角。
works.idea_en: For more-than-human design to reach practice, teachers need ready-to-use activities, not only research papers.
works.idea_zh: 超越人类的设计要走进实践，教师需要拿来即用的课堂活动，而不只是研究论文。
works.method: Classroom activities (likely developed in the authors' courses at Malmö, Aarhus and Eindhoven) structured into a teaching framework.
works.method_zh: 把课堂活动（很可能来自作者在马尔默、奥胡斯和埃因霍温的课程）整理成教学框架。

paper.title: More-than-Human Perspectives in Teaching Technology Design: From Research to Classroom, to the Real World?

works.title: Living Textiles: Microbial Biosensors and Textile Fluidics
works.description: A platform that integrates genetically engineered whole-cell bacterial biosensors into textiles, kept alive by fluid channels in the fabric, so garments can sense the body and environment and signal through visible material change.
works.description_zh: 一个把基因工程全细胞细菌生物传感器整合进纺织品的平台，依靠面料中的流体通道维持细胞存活，使衣物能感知身体与环境，并以可见的材料变化发出信号。
works.idea_en: Smart textiles without electronics: living cells do the sensing, and the fabric becomes a designed habitat.
works.idea_zh: 不用电子元件的智能纺织品：由活细胞完成感知，面料则成为被设计出来的栖所。
